newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU raids Opel/Mercedes in car pricing probe - source.
newsitem.headline: EU raids Opel/Mercedes in car pricing probe - source.

text.p: The European Commission has raided offices of German carmaker Mercedes and General Motors' Opel, an EU source told reporters on Friday.

The raids, in connection with alleged irregularities in vehicle pricing and distribution arrangements operated by the two manufacturers, were on similar grounds to current Commission investigations into Volkswagen and its subsidiary Audi the source said.
The raids "were conducted a while ago," the source, who asked not to be named, said.
News of the raids emerged as the Commission released details of car price differentials across 12 of the EU's 15 member countries, excluding Greece, Finland and Denmark.
Commission data up until November 1, 1996 showed that 23 of the EU's 75 best-selling models were cheapest in the Netherlands while 21 were cheapest in Portugal.

The Commission said parallel trade in cars, when customers try to buy vehicles elswehere in the EU when price differences make it attractive to do so, was being blocked in Germany, Belgium, Spain and the Netherlands.
"It was found that final customers still encounter obstacles in certain member states," it said in a statement.
Raids on Mercedes related to sales in all four named countries while those on Opel related only to Dutch sales, the source said.

If the Commission were to find the companies guilty of malpractice it could strip them of anti-trust exemptions related to their distribution agreements, a move which would open tightly restricted vehicle distribution arrangements to greater competition, the source said.
